<!-- pr-reviewer: d1dc959b69249d681a26b0916fa2f91e82d012cd -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One gap, and it is backstopped today, so this is not a silent gouge on `main`. A walk that passes straight *through* another chord at a vertex lying within `TOUCH` of that chord's line is no longer reported. The exact-sign check did report that case, and the decision file says it cannot happen.

Reviewed at head `d1dc959b`, trial-merged locally with `origin/main` 7e3c75f9 (clean merge, never pushed). Windows 11, x86_64.

### What looks good
- `crosses` / `side` are the exact-sign test with the zero widened to `|orient| <= TOUCH*|ab|`, which is a perpendicular-distance band of 1 pm around the other chord's **line**, as described. An exact T-touch was already "not proper" (sign 0), so per chord pair the change only widens "exactly on the line" to "within 1 pm of it". I confirmed this reading.
- Non-finite points are now reported first and always cross (the safe direction). Before, a NaN/inf `y` could slip past the old x-only bounds check. A zero-length chord gives `orient == 0` exactly, so it never crosses, the same as `proper`.
- The knife-edge pins also assert that the old `proper` tripped on at least one jitter, so the case is really exercised. The bucketed scan is cross-checked against all pairs.
- `lift_link` keeps `proper`, as stated. The verifier's law (a) (`sim/verify/laws.rs::proper_cross`) stays exact-sign, and the PR says so (#1129).
- Provenance comment present. `guard.rs` 151 lines, `guard_tests.rs` 210.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib adaptive` | 33 passed, 1 ignored |
| motion `adaptive_band` / `adaptive_hsm` / `adaptive_orbit_seam` / `pocket3d_hsm` / `rotary_adaptive` / `offset_shells` / `tiny_step` / `machining2d` (debug) | 2 / 1 (+5 ign) / 1 / 3 (+1 ign) / 3 (+3 ign) / 6 (+1 ign) / 3 / 66, all ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-app --test pocket3d_hsm -- --ignored` (heavy pin) | 1 passed in 195.9 s; pin **unchanged**: moves 16197, planar 15458, arcs 1581 (Windows exact triple) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test golden_cl` | 25 passed |

### Probes I ran (local only, removed afterwards)
| Probe | `proper` (old) | `crosses` / `first_crossing` (new) |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 mm lap crossed mid-chord at 1e-6 rad (ends 1e-4 mm off the line) | crosses | **crosses** |
| crossing 1e-6 mm deep, mid-chord | crosses | **crosses** |
| single chord ending 0.9 pm past a 1000 mm lap at 1e-6 rad | crosses | touch (overshoot along the chord ~0.9 µm, perpendicular 0.9 pm) |
| walk `(2,1) -> (2,-0.5e-9) -> (2,-1)` through lap `(0,0)-(4,0)` | **crosses** | **not reported** |
| same, vertex +0.5 pm | **crosses** | **not reported** |
| same, vertex exactly on the line | not reported | not reported |
| same at 1 m coordinates (lap y = 1000) | - | **not reported** |
| 1 µm chord at x = 1, 1000, 5000 mm, crossed 2 pm each side | - | crosses (noise stays below TOUCH) |

### The penetration bound
- **Per chord pair.** A pair is missed only if some end of one chord stands within δ = 1e-9 mm (perpendicular) of the other's line. Its perpendicular penetration is therefore ≤ 1 pm. Its overshoot measured along the chord is ≤ δ / sin θ. That reaches 1e-4 mm only when θ ≤ 1e-5 rad (about 2 arcsec) and the chord is at least that long. At those angles the old exact test was already decided by rounding noise. So per pair the bound holds, and it is harmless.
- **Per walk, it does not hold.** When the vertex shared by chords `c-d` and `d-e` lands in the band of chord `ab`'s interior, `c-d` reads as "ends on ab" and `d-e` reads as "starts on ab". Neither pair is reported, yet the walk passes through `ab` from one side to the other with unbounded depth (the probe above: 1 mm each side). Exact-sign had the same hole only for an exact zero, a measure-zero set. This PR widens it to a 2 pm band around every chord's line. The chance per crossing is small (~2e-9 mm / chord length), but it is not zero, and a vertex snapped onto another walk is exactly the kind of geometry the planner makes.
- **Scale (b).** `orient` is plain f64, with no robust-predicate crate. Its error is about eps·X·(|ab| + |ac|), so the distance noise is about 2e-13·(1 + |ac|/|ab|) mm at X = 1 m. That is below TOUCH unless one chord is over ~4500x shorter than its distance to the other point's end. So the fix does its job at metre scale, and where the noise wins it falls back to exact-sign-by-noise, as before.

### Requested before merge
1. **A walk passing through a chord at a vertex within `TOUCH` of that chord's interior must still be reported.** See `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard.rs:57-64` (`crosses`) and the scan at `:141`. Reproduction: `first_crossing(&[vec![(0,0),(4,0)], vec![(2,1),(2,-0.5e-9),(2,-1)]])` returns `None` on this head and `Some` with `proper`. Two possible fixes:
   - excuse an end that reads 0 only when it is within `TOUCH` of one of the other chord's **end points** (a shared vertex, the #1048 case). An interior T-contact keeps the exact sign.
   - or, when a vertex reads 0 against another chord's interior, report a crossing if that walk's previous and next points stand strictly on opposite sides (pass-through), and a touch if they stand on the same side (T-touch). The retrace case your decision file needs (collinear, `orient` exactly 0 along the whole run) is unaffected either way.

   Pin it with the probe above, at ±0.5 pm and at 1 m coordinates. Also correct the claim in `docs/decisions/1048-guard-shared-ends.md:29-31` ("can only meet the other chord at that end, so the most a hidden crossing could be is a 1 pm overlap") and in the `TOUCH` doc comment (`guard.rs:15-21`, "no self-cut of a cutter can hide inside it"). Both hold per chord pair, not per walk.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Downstream (d).** `first_crossing` feeds `pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes` (a crossing sends the level to Offset rings by name) and `pocket_troch::trochoid_passes` (it refuses the trochoid). `crossing_pairs` feeds `lift::coarsen` (a crossing keeps the fine chords). A pair no longer reported therefore keeps the adaptive plan or the coarse chords. Today the verifier's exact-sign law (a) still sees the pass-through above (the vertex is 0.5 pm off, not 0), so the post is refused by name rather than cut. That is why this is not a Prime-Directive blocker on `main`. **#1129 must not port `crosses` to the verifier as it stands.** If it did, the backstop would be gone and this would become a silent self-crossing.
- The along-chord overshoot at ultra-shallow angles (≤ 1e-5 rad) is the one place the per-pair band reaches 0.1 µm along the path. The perpendicular depth stays 1 pm, so I see no machining consequence.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Back to draft to fix the review on d1dc959b: the crossing guard's TOUCH band around the other chord's line hides a walk passing through a chord at a vertex a picometre off it. Switching to the end-point-only touch (same rule and constant as the verifier's CROSSING_TOUCH in #1129) and pinning the probe.

Review fixes pushed at `0f2f4217` (one commit on top of d1dc959b; trial-merge with upstream/main is clean).

**1. A walk through a chord at a vertex within TOUCH of its interior is reported again.**
`guard::crosses` now uses the end-point-only touch, the same rule and value as the verifier's `CROSSING_TOUCH` / `proper_cross_touch` (#1129, PR #1308). A chord end within `TOUCH` = 1e-9 mm (a point-to-point `hypot` distance) of one of the other chord's END points reads as on its line. Everywhere else the exact sign stays the law, so an interior T-contact a rounding past the chord crosses. `TOUCH` stays a local constant, and its doc comment points at the sim constant: motion takes no dependency on sim. Exact contacts (a vertex exactly on the interior, a collinear overlap, the retraced lifted chords of `a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses`) keep their exact-zero reading, unchanged.

- New pin: `a_walk_through_a_chord_at_a_vertex_a_picometre_off_its_line_still_crosses`. It covers your probe `(2,1) -> (2,±0.5e-9) -> (2,-1)` through lap `(0,0)-(4,0)` at origins (0,0), (37.25,-12.5), (1000,1000) and (-998.5,1001), checking both `first_crossing` and `crossing_pairs`, and also your exact reproduction.
- `a_contact_is_no_crossing_and_a_micron_past_is` now pins that a vertex -1e-12 / -5e-10 / -1e-6 past the interior crosses, while 0, +1e-12, +5e-10 and +1e-6 do not.
- The shared-vertex pins are unchanged and pass: the spiral returning to its seed, a return landing on a chord end, a ring starting on the previous ring's vertex, and a real crossing near a shared point.

**2. Corrected claims.** The `TOUCH` doc comment and `docs/decisions/1048-guard-shared-ends.md` no longer say "no self-cut can hide inside it" or "the most a hidden crossing could be is a 1 pm overlap". The decision file records the review, the per-walk hole, why it was withdrawn, and the residual. The residual is an exactly on-line vertex, which is unchanged from exact-sign and the same as the verifier.

**Gate (macOS arm64, debug, at 0f2f4217):**
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib adaptive` | 32 passed, 1 ignored (guard: 9 passed) |
| motion `adaptive_band` / `adaptive_hsm` / `adaptive_orbit_seam` / `pocket3d_hsm` / `rotary_adaptive` / `offset_shells` / `tiny_step` / `machining2d` | 2 / 1 (+5 ign) / 1 / 3 (+1 ign) / 2 (+3 ign) / 6 (+1 ign) / 3 / 66, all ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test golden_cl` | 25 passed |

Not run: the release-lane heavy pin `pocket3d_hsm --ignored`.

Coordination (UMA, mkinney fork agent): UMA is doing a local-only check of the delta since NeoTech's review d1dc959b, at head 0f2f4217. This is not a review, and nothing will be posted here from it (no marker, no labels). M3 and M5: please pick a different PR.

**Estimated agent cost to merge-ready (runs known to this session):** ~$0.69 (123k tokens, re-review, Opus 5.5); the first review's tokens are not known. Blended upper estimate (90 % input / 10 % output at list price). The author's own runs and main-session coordination aren't counted.

Follow-up for the author (not blocking): `guard::TOUCH` can be `crate::verify::CROSSING_TOUCH` directly - motion already depends on camcraft-sim (`crates/motion/Cargo.toml`), so the two constants cannot drift.
